en.title: The 2-hour rest rule ultra-long-haul Airbus A350 pilots follow before landing
en.summary: US federal rules for augmented operations require the pilot who will fly the landing to have two consecutive hours of in-flight rest available during the second half of the duty period. Singapore Airlines' Singapore–New York service, flown by four pilots over a roughly 20-hour duty period, shows how 8/8 and 6/8/2 rotations arrange that rest, while the A350's crew rest facility and the separate 40-minute controlled-rest rule follow the same logic.
body: Ultra-long-haul flying is scheduled backward from the landing. Under US federal rules for augmented operations, the pilot who will fly the aircraft during landing must have two consecutive hours of in-flight rest available during the second half of the flight duty period. The rule does not simply require pilots to rest; it specifies which pilot rests and when, based on the phase of the flight that pilot will be responsible for. An augmented crew carries more pilots than the aircraft's minimum certification requirement so one pilot can be replaced for in-flight rest, and the Federal Aviation Administration (FAA) also requires at least ten consecutive hours of rest, including at least eight uninterrupted hours of sleep opportunity, before a duty period begins.

Singapore Airlines operates Singapore to New York with four pilots — two captains and two first officers — across a duty period of roughly 20 hours, splitting into two pairs that take turns at the controls. The Points Guy described two ways to divide a flight of around 17.5 hours: an even 8/8 split giving each pair about eight hours of rest, and a 6/8/2 rotation that deliberately trims the relief crew's sleep so the operating crew returns to the flight deck roughly three hours before landing, leaving time to assess weather changes and operational updates. Either way, the handover is formal, with a briefing covering fuel, weather and traffic.

The Airbus A350's crew rest facility sits above the forward galley, reached through a hatch in the ceiling, and holds two bunks plus, depending on configuration, a reclining seat and an entertainment monitor; it is used only when three or more pilots are on duty. The FAA defines three classes of rest facility under 14 CFR Part 117: Class 1 is a bunk allowing a flat sleeping position, separate from the flight deck and passenger cabin, temperature-controlled, with crew control over lighting and isolation from noise; Class 2 is a cabin seat allowing a flat or near-flat position, separated from passengers by at least a curtain; Class 3 is a seat reclining at least 40 degrees with leg and foot support. The class sets the maximum flight duty period for augmented operations, with Class 1 allowing the longest; Class 1 sleeping surfaces measure 78 by 30 inches, with 35 cubic feet of space around them plus a communal area of 65 cubic feet.

"Controlled rest" — a pilot napping in the seat on the flight deck while the other pilot remains at the controls — follows different rules. Flight Safety Foundation guidance caps it at 40 minutes to minimize sleep inertia, requires a recovery period of at least 20 minutes with no part in flight duties or briefings, and states that recovery and the following briefing should be completed at least 30 minutes before the top of descent. The FAA does not authorize in-seat cockpit naps for Part 121 operations, while EASA and many other authorities permit controlled rest under defined conditions. The shared logic is sleep inertia, the transitory impairment of alertness after waking: the 40-minute cap keeps a napping pilot out of slow-wave sleep, and the two-hour rule and the 6/8/2 rotation alike leave a gap between waking and the most demanding phase of flight.

zh.title: 空中巴士A350超長程機師落地前2小時休息規定解析
zh.summary: 美國聯邦航空規章要求，超長程增員航班中負責落地的機師，須在值勤後半段享有連續2小時機上休息；新加坡航空新加坡—紐約航線以4名機師、約20小時值勤為例，透過8/8或6/8/2輪替安排休息；機上休息艙等級與駕駛艙內40分鐘可控休息各有不同規範。
body: 超長程航班的機師休息安排，是從落地那一刻往回推算的。美國聯邦航空規章針對增員組員運作規定，負責落地階段的機師必須在值勤期的後半段，享有連續2小時的機上休息。這項規定不只是要求機師休息，而是明確規定由哪一位機師、在什麼時段休息，取決於他在航班最後階段負責的任務。增員組員是指機上機師人數超過飛機最低認證需求，讓機師可以輪替離開駕駛艙休息；值勤開始前，美國聯邦航空總署另要求至少連續10小時休息，其中包含至少8小時不受打擾的睡眠機會。
新加坡航空新加坡—紐約航線以4名機師執行、值勤期約20小時，分為兩組輪流執勤與休息。據《The Points Guy》描述，約17.5小時的航班有兩種排班方式：8/8輪替讓兩組各休息約8小時；6/8/2輪替則刻意縮減替補組員的睡眠，讓執勤組員在落地前約3小時回到駕駛艙，以便有時間掌握天氣變化與營運更新。無論採用哪種方式，換班時都須進行正式交接，內容涵蓋燃油、天氣與航路交通。

空中巴士A350的機組休息艙位於前方廚房上方，經由天花板艙門進入，內有2張睡鋪，依構型另有可調座椅與娛樂螢幕，僅在3名以上機師值勤時使用。美國聯邦航空總署將休息設施分為3級：第1級為可平躺的睡鋪，與駕駛艙及客艙分隔、具溫度控制與燈光控制並隔絕噪音；第2級為客艙內可平躺或近乎平躺的座椅，至少以布簾與乘客分隔；第3級為駕駛艙或客艙內可傾斜至少40度並提供腿足支撐的座椅。設施等級決定增員運作的最長值勤時間，第1級允許最長的值勤期；A350的雙睡鋪休息艙符合第1級描述，其睡鋪尺寸為78×30英吋、周圍空間35立方英尺，另有65立方英尺的共用進出空間。

駕駛艙內的「可控休息」則是另一套程序：機師在座位上小睡、另一名機師保持操控，依飛航安全基金會指引以40分鐘為上限，之後須有至少20分鐘恢復期，期間不參與任何值勤或簡報，且恢復期與簡報須在下降頂點前至少30分鐘完成。這套做法並非各地通用：美國聯邦航空總署不允許第121部營運的駕駛艙內座位小睡，但歐洲航空安全局與許多其他主管機關在明確條件下允許。兩套規則背後的共同邏輯是「睡眠慣性」——剛睡醒時的短暫警覺與表現下降；40分鐘上限避免機師進入深睡，而2小時規定與6/8/2輪替同樣讓機師在落地前留出清醒緩衝。
